title: Simply supported plate buckling
description: Square plate a=b=1 m, t=0.01 m, E=210 GPa, nu=0.3; 5x5 shell mesh.
geometry: 36 nodes; 25 elements. Square plate a=b=1 m, t=0.01 m, E=210 GPa, nu=0.3; 5x5 shell mesh.
material: E=2.1e+11, nu=0.3; shell thickness=0.01. SI: m, N, kg, s, Pa
boundary_conditions: All edges transverse displacement fixed; left edge axial displacement fixed; one Y anchor; uniform 1 Pa compressive axial stress.
loading: Uniform 1 Pa reference compression, applied as consistent edge nodal forces; multiplier equals critical stress numerically in Pa.

references.citation: Timoshenko and Gere, Theory of Elastic Stability, 2nd ed. (1961), plate buckling.
Wierzbicki, T. MIT 2.080J Structural Mechanics, Lecture 11: Buckling of Plates and Sections (2013).

observations: The supplied input omitted SPC selection from the buckling subcase. This rerun explicitly adds SPC=1 to that subcase, preserving the intended constraints. The original failed attempt is retained in the audit record.
limits: Linear elasticity and small-displacement equilibrium or linearized bifurcation/modal analysis; this is computational verification, not a material-test validation.
figure_caption: Recorded JFEM result; deformation is amplified, mode amplitudes/signs arbitrary. Green triangles mark constrained nodes; magenta arrows mark available point loads.
